operators.name: max_dim_keepdim_forward

parameters.name: x
parameters.shape: same as input; expected [B, H, W] but kernel should support arbitrary dims

items.shape: same as x with dim reduced to 1 if keepdim else removed
same as x with dim reduced to 1 if keepdim else removed

semantics: Computes max along specified dim, returning max values and corresponding indices (as int64).
Matches torch.max(x, dim=1, keepdim=True): reduction over dimension 1 of the input tensor.
keepdim=True means the reduced dimension is retained with size 1.
For ties, returns the first occurrence index (as torch.max does).
Output tensors have same dtype and device as input, except indices are int64.
Input may be non-contiguous; kernel should handle strides.

operators.name: cosine_similarity_dim_forward

parameters.name: x2
parameters.shape: same as reference max_values (broadcastable with x1 along dim)

returns.shape: same as x1 with dim removed

semantics: Computes cosine similarity between x1 and x2 along the specified dim, following broadcasting rules.
Matches F.cosine_similarity(x, max_values, dim=1): x shape [64,8192,128], max_values shape [64,1,128], output [64,128].
Formula: dot(x1, x2, dim) / (||x1||_dim * ||x2||_dim).
For each batch b and column c (out index), computes over the height dimension.
Uses epsilon 1e-8 in denominator to avoid division by zero, as PyTorch does.
Input x1 and x2 may have different strides; kernel should handle broadcasting and non-contiguity.
Reduces input x of shape [64,8192,128] along dim=1 (height) to max values and indices.
Output max_values shape [64,1,128], indices shape [64,1,128] int64.
Indices are global indices along dim=1 (0..8191).
Tie-breaking: first index wins.
Computes cosine similarity between x and max_values along dim=1.
x shape [64,8192,128], max_values shape [64,1,128] (broadcast along dim=1).
Output shape [64,128].
For each batch b and column c, numerator = sum_{h} x[b,h,c] * max_values[b,0,c]; denominator = sqrt(sum x^2) * sqrt(sum max_values^2).
max_values already has size 1 in dim=1, so sum over h just multiplies by 8192? No, here sum over h of max_values[b,0,c]^2 = 8192 * max_values[b,0,c]^2, since it broadcasts.
Returns the similarity tensor of shape [64,128].
